newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan shares bounce on Fazio, end 0.46 pct down.
newsitem.headline: Milan shares bounce on Fazio, end 0.46 pct down.

text.p: Italian shares ended weaker on Thursday after a lacklustre session but recovered from their lows after Bank of Italy Governor Antonio Fazio said interest rates could fall faster if the 1997 budget is fully implemented.
"We've seen some recovery after Fazio's comments on interest rates, even if the threat of a bigger-than-expected budget overshoot put the brakes on enthusiasm," said one trader.
The all-share Mibtel index ended down 0.46 percent at 9,902 after an earlier low of 9,832. The Mib30 blue-chip index closed off 0.30 percent at 14,900, off its day's low of 14,775.
Fazio told a parliamentary budget committee that "if the corrective budget finds full and swift implementation, the fall in (rates) could be more rapid".
But he added that Italy's 1996 public deficit may overshoot the original 113 trillion lire target by up to 20 trillion lire.
Traders said a parliamentary defeat on Wednesday night for the government hit sentiment. "The market started weak after the government defeat but it recovered some losses," said one.
Former Olivetti chief Carlo De Benedetti's financial holding company Cofide was one of a handful of shares to buck the downward trend to finish 6.14 percent up at 595 lire.
Telecom Italia finished 1.97 percent down at 3,331 and Gemina, hit by news that ex-officials of the financial holding group were being arrested, fell 2.08 percent to close at 704.7.

Fiat finished off 0.5 percent at 4,146 on sluggish new Italian car registration figures. Official data released earlier showed Fiat's new registrations were down 17.5 percent year-on-year in September.

Overall, dealers said the quiet market mood should continue ahead of the weekend. "It's been rather quiet, but the market's had a good run. It's healthy for it to come back a bit," one dealer said. "I don't expect too much action tomorrow." REUTER
